articles.title: Long-term review: six months with a folding phone
articles.subtitle: The hinge held up, but habits didn't fully change
articles.excerpt: After half a year of daily use, here's what actually changed about how we use a phone that folds in half, and what didn't.
articles.author: admin

content.text: Overview
After half a year of daily use, here's what actually changed about how we use a phone that folds in half, and what didn't.
The hinge held up

The hinge held up, but habits didn't fully change. After half a year and an estimated 40,000 individual folds, there's no perceptible looseness and the crease is only visible under direct light at a steep angle.

What did change was expectations: within the first month, the novelty of the larger inner screen wore off, and by month three the phone was mostly used folded closed, exactly like a conventional phone, for roughly 80% of interactions.
Battery over time

Battery capacity measured at the six-month mark had dropped to about 94% of its original rating, which is in line with a standard non-folding flagship over the same period and better than we expected given the more complex internal layout.
The fold stopped being a party trick around week two and just became the phone.
Our take

It's an encouraging sign for where the category is headed next, even if not every question has been answered yet — we still want to see a second and third year of use before calling folding durability solved.

articles.title: Review: the noise-cancelling earbuds that finally got comfortable
articles.subtitle: Small design tweaks make a big difference
articles.excerpt: After years of earbuds that fell out during a run, this pair finally nails the fit without sacrificing sound quality.
articles.author: ashraf

content.text: Overview
After years of earbuds that fell out during a run, this pair finally nails the fit without sacrificing sound quality.
The details

Small design tweaks make a big difference. After years of earbuds that fell out during a run, this pair finally nails the fit without sacrificing sound quality, thanks mostly to a new four-size tip set and a shell that sits lower in the ear canal.

In our stability testing, the earbuds survived 40 minutes of interval sprints and a full studio dance class without a single reseat, which is more than we can say for the previous generation or for most competitors in this price range.

Active noise cancelling is rated at up to 32dB of reduction, and in practice it flattens most office chatter and subway rumble, though sharp transient sounds like keyboard clacks still get through at the edges.
Battery and case
Rated battery life is 7 hours per charge with noise cancelling on, or 9.5 hours with it off, and the case adds three additional full charges before it needs to be plugged in itself.
This is the first pair in this price bracket we've genuinely forgotten we were wearing.
Our take
It's an encouraging sign for where the category is headed next, even if not every question has been answered yet — durability over multiple years is still an open question we plan to revisit.

articles.title: Wireless charging pads finally stopped overheating
articles.subtitle: A small fix that took years to arrive
articles.excerpt: Early wireless chargers ran hot enough to trigger phones' thermal throttling mid-charge. A new generation of coil designs has quietly fixed the problem.
articles.author: admin

content.text: Overview
Early wireless chargers ran hot enough to trigger phones' thermal throttling mid-charge. A new generation of coil designs has quietly fixed the problem.
What actually changed
Newer pads spread the charging coil's heat across a wider surface instead of concentrating it under the phone, cutting peak temperatures by a noticeable margin.
Firmware improvements on the phone side also help, pacing the charge rate before heat becomes an issue rather than reacting after the fact.
Our take
It's a small, unglamorous fix, but one that makes wireless charging finally feel as reliable as plugging in a cable.

commentsList.text: Good to know, my old pad used to get uncomfortably warm.

articles.title: Budget earbuds that quietly beat the flagship pair
articles.subtitle: Sometimes the cheaper option is the better one
articles.excerpt: A side-by-side test found the mid-range earbuds matched or beat their flagship sibling on call quality and battery life, for less than half the price.
articles.author: ashraf

content.text: Overview
A side-by-side test found the mid-range earbuds matched or beat their flagship sibling on call quality and battery life, for less than half the price.
How the test worked
Both pairs were used for two weeks of daily calls and commutes, with battery life logged after each full charge cycle.
The budget pair's microphone array handled wind noise noticeably better, likely due to a simpler but more conservative noise-gating algorithm.
Our take
The flagship pair still wins on app features and case design, but on the fundamentals, the cheaper pair is hard to argue against.
